company_name: TS Financial Holding (formerly Taishin Financial Holdings)

evidence.activity: Taishin Arts Award, run by the company-backed arts foundation, funds and recognises contemporary visual, performing and interdisciplinary artists
evidence.quote: With a cumulative award prize of NT$3.5 million, the awards offer the largest sum in support of Taiwanese contemporary arts.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Arts and Culture Development > Taishin Arts Award

creativity.criterion: level 3: ongoing exhibition program for artists with disclosed count

creativity.criterion: level 3: named arts-education program with participant numbers

evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Arts and Culture Development > Art & Sustainability—2025 Audible City Episode

creativity.criterion: level 2: specific commissioned performance project, limited reach

evidence.activity: Free financial literacy courses designed for artists and creative teams
evidence.quote: The courses were attended by approximately 140 art professionals to great acclaim.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Arts and Culture Development > Basic Financial Courses for Art Professionals

creativity.criterion: level 2: direct support to artists, limited reach

community.criterion: level 2: external skills program, limited reach

evidence.activity: Employee arts courses covering art appreciation, theatre and arts films
evidence.quote: A total of 19 employee arts courses took place in 2025.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Arts and Culture Development > Employee arts courses

evidence.activity: Taishin Charity Foundation 'Power of Love' public-vote grant program for non-profits
evidence.quote: Over the past 16 years, a total of more than NT$420 million in charity funds has been used, benefiting 2,008 non-profit organizations and 6.56 million beneficiaries.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Charity and Welfare > The "Power of Love"
evidence.indicators: more than NT$420 million; 2,008 non-profit organizations; 6.56 million beneficiaries

community.criterion: level 3: named grant program with dollars and beneficiaries disclosed

evidence.activity: Taishin Youth Foundation volunteer platform and annual Youth Volunteer Awards working with schools and charities
evidence.quote: The foundation also has long-term relationships with the central government (the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Health and Welfare) and 22 municipal governments, more than 1,200 middle schools, and close to 100 charitable organizations and local volunteering centers.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Charity and Welfare > Taishin Youth Volunteer Awards
evidence.indicators: 1,830 youth service stories; 22 municipal governments; more than 1,200 middle schools; close to 100 charitable organizations

community.criterion: level 3: named youth program partnering with schools, with reach figures

evidence.activity: Industry-academia internship program for university and vocational students
evidence.quote: In 2025, about 600 students were recruited into an internship program.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Academic exchange

community.criterion: level 3: external internship program with participant numbers

evidence.activity: Scholarships and summer internships for financially disadvantaged National Taiwan University students
evidence.quote: As part of its commitment to the community and talent development, the Company offers scholarships and summer internships for National Taiwan University students from financially disadvantaged back-grounds.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Academic exchange

evidence.activity: Charity golf tournaments raising donations
evidence.quote: Taishin has also hosted charity golf tournaments since 2011, with a total of 703 participants and more than NT$24.6 million raised in charitable donations.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Sports sponsorship

community.criterion: level 2: specific community fundraising with figures

evidence.activity: Support for the Nantou County Youth Karate Team via customer donations
evidence.quote: Taishin began supporting the Nantou County Youth Karate Team in 2005, calling upon customers through the PayEasy online platform to participate in small-amount and receipt donations, with cumulative donations exceeding NT$119.26 million.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate responsibility > Sports sponsorship

community.criterion: level 3: ongoing youth sports support with dollar figures

evidence.activity: Taishin University structured employee training and learning platform
evidence.quote: By integrating Taishin University with the CTMS, the company is able to incorporate managerial skill training with general education and other relevant courses, so that each employee may study on their own in a systematically structured course design.
evidence.section: Annual report > Employees > Taishin University

evidence.activity: Nationwide ATM upgrade adding enlarged-font and barrier-free cardless withdrawal for elderly and visually impaired customers
evidence.quote: Taishin Bank has comprehensively upgraded nearly 4,000 ATMs nationwide, adding “enlarged font” and “barrier-free cardless withdrawal” features.
evidence.section: Annual report > Risk management > Emerging risks > Optimize financial services for the elderly and ensure inclusive finance

cross_cultural.criterion: level 3: named accessibility program with numbers

evidence.activity: Multilingual ATM interface and accessible ATMs for visually impaired customers
evidence.quote: The user interface was already available in Chinese and English, and a total of seven new languages including Japanese, Korean, Thai, Vietnamese, and Indonesian were added over time
evidence.section: Annual report > Operating Status > Business plans > ATM

evidence.activity: Online lost-card reporting usable by cardholders with hearing or speech impairments
evidence.quote: This feature enables cardholders with hearing or speech impairments to handle the process independently without having to make a phone call, thereby significantly improving financial inclusiveness.
evidence.section: Annual report > Operating Status > Credit card business > 2025

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: specific accessibility feature, limited reach

evidence.activity: Employee stress-relief workshop staffed by hired blind masseurs
evidence.quote: Taishin Holdings hires blind masseurs and masseuses to help employees relieve work stress, creating a happy and healthy work environment while contributing towards charity.
evidence.section: Annual report > Corporate Governance Report > Employee rights and wellness

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: inclusion of people with disabilities, no figures

evidence.activity: English version of the bank app to widen access
evidence.quote: At the same time, it is committed to advancing inclusive finance by developing an English version of the APP to deliver inclusive financial services.
evidence.section: Annual report > Operating Status > Digital Banking Business

evidence.activity: Venture capital subsidiaries invest in start-ups and link them to group financing and listing services
evidence.quote: Venture capital companies first discover potential start-up companies, then commercial banks provide financing, and securities underwriters provide TWSE/TPEx listing services, so that the synergy and integration benefits of financial services can be brought into play.
evidence.section: Annual report > Operating Status > Taishin Venture Capital > Business scope > Financial integration

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 2: specific start-up financing service, no reach figures

evidence.activity: Ordinary SME lending
evidence.quote: The outstanding balance of SME loans reached NT$227 billion, an increase of NT$23.8 billion from 2024, representing a growth rate of 11.7%.
evidence.section: Annual report > Letter to Shareholders > Wholesale Banking Services

evidence.activity: Standardised working-capital loan approval for micro enterprises
evidence.quote: In terms of micro enterprise service, we have established standardized approval processes to efficiently assist businesses in obtaining operating working capital, thereby achieving inclusive finance.
evidence.section: Annual report > Operating Status > Business plans > Micro enterprise service

creativity.reason: Level 3: named, ongoing arts programs (Taishin Arts Award, concerts, exhibitions, lecture series) with disclosed figures, but not a major business line.

community.reason: Level 3: external community investment and education with substantial measured reach (Power of Love NT$420 million to 2,008 NPOs, 1,200+ schools, 600 interns), not central to strategy.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 3: named accessibility program with numbers (nearly 4,000 ATMs upgraded) plus multilingual and disability-access services, not a major business line.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 2: venture capital financing of start-ups is a specific enabling service with no reach figures; SME lending itself counts only as serving.

ai.notes: The company merged with Shin Kong Financial Holding (Shin Kong Life joined in July 2025), so headcounts and some figures reflect the combined group. The arts and charity programs run through affiliated foundations (Taishin Bank Foundation for Arts and Culture, Taishin Charity Foundation, Taishin Youth Foundation); these were credited as company activities. Several figures are cumulative over many years: Power of Love over 16 years, Arts Award over 23 years, karate donations since 2005. The 'Caring Taiwan' rice project (NT$ 46.06 million) was left out because the text does not show whether it is still operating. An arts sponsorship figure stated as 'close to over millions' is too vague to use. The English app is recorded as planned. Products for vulnerable groups (elderly, disabled, indigenous, young) are described as future intentions only. Board gender diversity and overseas service to 'the global Chinese community' were not scored. Large SME loan balances (NT$227 billion and NT$336 billion) count only as serving. The text states there was no human rights violation in 2025.
